subject: Mutual action plan & capacity reservation — Aperture Therapeutics
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@aperturetx.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Gordon Lee <gordon.lee@aperturetx.com>, procurement@aperturetx.com
Date: Sun, 07 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aperture MAP kickoff — capacity needs and timelines

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Aperture is excited about Redwood’s latency profile and the private deployment options. Procurement asked me to capture the high level asks so we can align on a mutual action plan (MAP) and procurement timeline. High-level asks from Infra + Procurement: 

- Lead time confirmation for Dedicated vs Private (H100 vs A100 availability).
- A conservative GPU pool sizing for our Phase 1 (inference for 40M monthly tokens, peak 250 QPS), plus a recommended growth buffer.
- What gating items will block an MSA / PO: SOC2 details, acceptance testing window, and on-prem install checklist.

Can you send a one-page MAP and a short evaluation plan? Ideal close window for us is mid-July, but procurement will escalate to Aug if lead times push out.

Best,
Samira Khan
Director, Platform Engineering
Aperture Therapeutics
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@aperturetx.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture MAP kickoff — capacity needs and timelines

Samira — thanks, and great framing. Draft attached: MAP_Aperture_v1.xlsx (summary sheet + acceptance milestones), and a quick GPU sizing csv that walks through conservative/typical/optimistic pools. Key notes up front: 

- Lead times: Hosted (immediate), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity on shared infra): typical lead ~4–6 weeks to reserve tranche; Dedicated with private tenancy for single-tenant GPU pools (Private): 10–12 weeks (procurement + networking + acceptance). These are our current estimates based on vendor procurement and rack availability.
- Sizing: For your stated 40M monthly tokens and 250 QPS peak we recommend starting with a 6-card H100 pool (balanced across two nodes) with autoscale burst to an additional 2 cards for spikes. Conservative path (for cost control): 4-card quantized A100 pool (recommended only if you accept ~5–10% quality variance).
- Acceptance/testing: 7 business day acceptance window post-cutover with a pre-agreed prompt/eval set. SOC2 artifacts: scope + AWS evidence + logging matrix included (SOC2_scope-evidence.pdf).

Next steps I propose: 
1) Review attached MAP and sizing with Infra (Gordon) this week.
2) We’ll lock a Draft PO + mutual milestones in HubSpot and circulate a DocuSign MSA to Procurement.
3) Run a 3-day evaluation (staging) with a representative eval workload — we’ll provide tooling and cost estimates.

Laura — can you add an acceptance checklist and estimated SLOs to the MAP? Marissa, can you confirm discounting/commit steps if they take Dedicated reserved capacity vs private?

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@aperturetx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture MAP kickoff — capacity needs and timelines

Samira, Diego — attaching an acceptance checklist inside the MAP and copying key gating items here: 

- Network readiness: VPC peering / VPN test, firewall rules list, and static IP allowlist.
- Data controls: encryption at rest verified, KMS integration confirmed.
- Performance acceptance: run 3 scripted eval scenarios (latency median/p95 target) and a token-fidelity regression on the provided prompt set.
- Rollback plan: snapshot of model versioning + config to revert to baseline.

Acceptance window: recommend 5 business days for basic functional tests and 7 business days if they run the full eval suite. If procurement needs an earlier close, we can compress to a 3-day smoke test for critical flows.

Also included: a checklist for onsite install ops for Private deployments (power, colocation handoff, and model weights transfer checklist).

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: procurement@aperturetx.com, Samira Khan <samira.khan@aperturetx.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture MAP kickoff — capacity needs and timelines

Hi Samira / Procurement — two quick datapoints from pricing operations to inform PO vs Reserved vs Private decisions: 

- Reserved Dedicated commit pricing (monthly) can reduce unit costs ~22% vs on-demand hosted pricing for token volumes in your range. We can tier further with a 12-month commit.
- Private (single-tenant) carries a higher base platform fee (one-time onboarding + recurring infra) and a longer lead time (10–12 weeks). We’ll include a specific tranche schedule in the MAP so procurement can attach milestones to PO payments.

Karthik — can you include a short quantization-quality comparison for A100 vs H100 for the suggested small (4–6 card) pools? Also flag any model variants we’d recommend for the 250 QPS traffic pattern.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@aperturetx.com>, Gordon Lee <gordon.lee@aperturetx.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 16:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture MAP kickoff — capacity needs and timelines

Samira / Gordon — quick technical summary and suggested acceptance load: 

- Recommendation: Start with 6x H100 (mixed precision) split across 2 nodes (3 cards/node) to meet 250 QPS headroom with p95 latency target < 220ms for the primary model. Keep an autoscale pool of +2 cards for burst capacity.
- Cost/quality tradeoff: 4x A100 quantized pool provides ~30–40% lower cost but expect a measurable fidelity delta on long-form generation and multi-turn state handling. I recommend running a 48-hour A/B eval in staging if cost is a gating factor.
- Acceptance test plan (staging): 
  * Day 1: integration smoke (connectivity, auth, KMS).
  * Day 2: throughput ramp (synthetic traffic to 80% peak) and latency profiling.
  * Day 3: eval sets and regression checks on critical prompt families.

I’ve uploaded a small script and the sizing csv to the Drive link in the MAP. If you want, we can schedule a short infra call tomorrow to validate VPC routing and peering.

Karthik Iyer
Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
